question_text:
A box of chocolates contains 6 dark brown, 4 light brown, and 2 white truffles. Two truffles are selected from the box without replacement.
Find the probability of selecting:

subparts.solution:
$$\text{P}(2 \text{ white truffles}) = \text{P}(\text{first is white} \cap \text{second is white})$$
$$= \text{P}(\text{first is white}) \times \text{P}(\text{second is white given first is white})$$
$$= \frac{2}{12} \times \frac{1}{11}$$
$$= \frac{2}{132}$$
$$= \frac{1}{66}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Sampling without replacement reduces both the number of favorable items and the total number of items by 1 for the second draw.
step_by_step: Probability the first truffle is white: $\frac{2}{12}$.
Probability the second truffle is white given the first is white: $\frac{1}{11}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Assuming sampling with replacement and using $\frac{2}{12} \times \frac{2}{12}$.

subparts.solution:
$$\text{P}(2 \text{ white truffles}) = \frac{1}{66} \quad \{\text{from a}\}$$
$$\text{P}(2 \text{ dark brown truffles}) = \text{P}(\text{first is dark brown}) \times \text{P}(\text{second is dark brown given first is dark brown})$$
$$= \frac{6}{12} \times \frac{5}{11} = \frac{30}{132} = \frac{5}{22}$$
$$\text{P}(2 \text{ light brown truffles}) = \text{P}(\text{first is light brown}) \times \text{P}(\text{second is light brown given first is light brown})$$
$$= \frac{4}{12} \times \frac{3}{11} = \frac{12}{132} = \frac{1}{11}$$
$$\text{P}(\text{different coloured truffles}) = 1 - \text{P}(\text{same coloured truffles})$$
$$= 1 - \left(\frac{1}{66} + \frac{5}{22} + \frac{1}{11}\right)$$
$$= 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The complement of 'different colours' when picking 2 items is 'same colours'.
step_by_step: Calculate probabilities of getting two of each colour without replacement.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Trying to sum all different color pairs individually, which is longer and more error-prone than using the complement.
